steps.speaker: Train Attendant
steps.content: Please make way! The doctor is here!
The crowd divides, barely creating a narrow path. The attendant pushes through, visibly tense, followed by that strange woman with the skeleton frame from earlier—Forensica.

Only now do you take a proper look at her. That wrinkled coat is covered in small tools and labels. Outside the context of the skeleton incident, it does look more like work attire. At the very least, it makes far more sense in a professional setting than that oversized suitcase did.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Step aside. Don't contaminate the scene.
She ignores the stares around her and walks straight toward the body, unfolding a pair of disposable gloves as she goes. She puts them on in a clean motion, then tightens them at the wrists.
She crouches down and carefully observes the body's condition. She then undresses it, exposing the torso, and begins examining the wounds in detail.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: ...Left chest, fourth intercostal space, clean wounds... Right hand, sharp weapon...
The second wound is below the right ribs, the third... She examines, confirms, and records each wound in detail. The entire process is seamless.

She's incredibly focused, her fingers moving with precision and efficiency. For a moment, you're almost dumbfounded—it's hard to imagine that this calm, composed doctor is the same person as the eccentric woman lugging a skeleton around earlier.

Just then, a bulky figure pushes through the crowd. The potbellied man glances at the scene, then immediately turns his head away. He pulls out a handkerchief to wipe the sweat from his brow, though his mouth doesn't stop running.

steps.speaker: Train Conductor
steps.content: How did the person die? Any conclusions yet? Can you tell who the killer is? How old are they? Are they male or female? The murderer isn't still on the train... right?
Forensica doesn't look up. She pulls out a high-intensity flashlight and directs the beam onto the body.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: ...D-3PO's talking again.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: "Oh great, someone's yapping. Can't he just shut up?"

steps.speaker: Train Conductor
steps.content: ...Who?

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: D-3PO. He's a good guy, because when L*** is working, he knows to keep quiet and stay in the background...
Forensica mutters without looking up, though her hands are moving noticeably faster now. The conductor scratches his head, clearly unable to follow her logic. You decide to speak up then.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: I believe what she's saying is that she needs a quiet environment when she's working. We should give her some space.

steps.speaker: Train Conductor
steps.content: It's not like it's some surgery though... That person's already dead...
Forensica flicks her wrist, and the high-intensity flashlight shines directly into the Conductor's eyes.
Actions speak louder than words, as they say. The Conductor squints, mutters a few complaints, and finally retreats. Silence returns to the scene once more.
Twenty minutes later, the coroner stands up. She tears a page from her notebook and hands it to you casually, just like when she shoved that business card into your hand earlier.

Estimated Time of Death: Approximately between 00:00-01:30. Margin of error may vary depending on ambient temperature, victim's physiology, and clothing. External Injury Overview: Twelve penetrating wounds from sharp weapon(s) observed across the body, primarily in the anterior chest region. Wounds are clean and sharp, consistent with injuries caused by single-edged and/or double-edged bladed weapon(s). No significant blunt force trauma observed elsewhere on the body. Cause of Death: Cardiac and/or major vascular rupture caused by penetration, resulting in acute exsanguination.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: The wounds are concentrated around the front of the chest. The pattern is chaotic with varying depths. Three of the stabs went extremely deep, my guess is those were the fatal ones. The rest are shallower, and two are barely more than scratches.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: What does that tell us? Are we looking at two attackers with different levels of strength?

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Can't say for certain. It's also possible the killer deliberately used varying force to throw off the investigation.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Though... what I can confirm is that the victim had already lost consciousness when the murder took place. Judging from the wounds, there was virtually no resistance.
The coroner's findings are thorough and precise, contrary to her earlier careless attitude.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Impressive. As expected of a professional.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: ...It's just basic forensics.
She rolls her eyes, as if you just said something absurd.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: I'm just relaying what the corpse told me. There's nothing difficult about that.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Is that so? Then I suppose I lack the talent for that particular language.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: As a detective, I've seen plenty of people who either screamed at the sight of a corpse, or... developed an unhealthy fascination with them.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Not many people can treat them with such composure. I can tell that you truly respect them.
The words catch her off guard. She turns her face away and falls silent for a moment.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: ...That's because they deserve it.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: The living come in all sorts—good, bad, idiots, liars. But the dead are equal. A corpse is just a corpse, after all. They don't lie, they have no bias, and their honesty is absolute.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: Listen to them, and they'll give you the truth. It's the most effective form of communication there is.

She speaks quietly, and for some reason, it reminds you of the way she looked at those bones in the corridor earlier. She has that same calm, gentle gaze. It seems she reserves all her harshness and caustic remarks for the living.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: It seems I've met an exceptionally skilled forensic pathologist then.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: Please, allow me to introduce myself. I happen to take on detective work from time to time. Perhaps we'll have the chance to work together in the future.
The woman hesitates for a moment before slowly nodding. Seizing the opportunity, you continue.

steps.speaker: Chief
steps.content: By the way, did you work at the city's Forensic Research Institute before? I've actually met a few of your former colleagues. They were all quite impressive—
The moment the words leave your mouth, you notice Forensica's expression instantly darkening.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: That's none of your concern.

steps.speaker: Forensica
steps.content: There's no point discussing this. The forensic report is complete. If you don't have anything else to say, I'll be taking my leave here.
She turns and disappears into the crowd without giving you a chance to respond.

You stand there, replaying your words in your head for a moment. In theory, you don't seem to have said anything offensive. But theory and reality rarely align. Clearly, something you said struck a nerve.
You're still puzzled, but the truth remains elusive. Though right now, the case takes priority over understanding why Forensica reacted that way.
You shake off the thought and return your focus to the case.
